2.text: The ceremonial usually lasts only one day; but sometimes it is repeated

3.text: the next morning, when the people say that it has lasted over night.

4.text: The arrangement of the ceremonial admits of several variations. Several

5.text: combinations of heads are used in it, such as one of walrus, one of thong-

6.text: seal, and one of ringed seal; or one of walrus, one of wild reindeer, and

7.text: one of hare; or two of walrus and two of wild reindeer; or one of walrus,

8.text: one of ringed seal, and one of white fox; etc. The heads are either placed

9.text: on the ground in the centre of the house, or are hung by a string under

10.text: the vent-hole. Several lighted lamps are put by their side, often a lamp for

13.text: pointed pole is firmly fastened in the centre of the house, so that its end

14.text: protrudes through the vent-hole, Various objects of thanksgiving are fastened

15.text: to the pole, such as a set of antlers, a skin of peltry, several coils of new

16.text: thongs, etc. During the ceremonial the male members of the family shoot

19.text: The same ceremonial may be arranged outdoors. Then it is called

20.text: “spear-house ceremonial” (poiˊhɪ-ra-mñêˊɪrg̣ɪn). Then a real spear, or a spear-

21.text: like pole, is stuck into the ground, and made fast in its place by several

22.text: lines supporting it from all sides, and tied to large stones lying on the ground.
